plain_english_policy: This bill amends the state's education funding structure for fiscal year 2010. It shifts $8 million of debt service payments (specifically for General Obligation Bonds Series 2005-A) from the Capital Improvement Trust Fund to the Education Trust Fund, while reducing funds available in the former source by that same amount. Additionally, it sets a specific cap ($11,028,645) on how much food stamp administration revenue can be reverted back to education; any excess unspent money must instead be used for subsidized child care slots.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would result in the Education Trust Fund absorbing additional debt service obligations previously covered by other state funds, effectively increasing its outflow. Simultaneously, it redirects surplus food stamp administrative revenues away from reverting to education and toward funding specific subsidized child care programs.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors advanced a bill that reallocates existing state funds between debt service obligations (shifting burden from Capital Improvement Trust Fund to Education Trust Fund) and redirects surplus food stamp revenues toward child care subsidies rather than reverting them to the education fund.
evidence_quotes: to amend the fiscal year 2010 Education Appropriation Bill (Act 2009-339) by changing a portion of the funding source on the General Obligation Bonds, 2005-A from the Capital Improvement Trust Fund to the Education Trust Fund

the maximum amount of funds from the sales tax for the administration of the Food Stamp Program that may be reverted by the Department of Human Resources to the Education Trust Fund shall be $11,028,645 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2010. Any such funds over this amount not utilized in the Food Stamp Program shall be expended for subsidized child care slots
